The establishment is situated in close proximity to Grant Road Station, specifically on the first floor of the Krishna Palace Hotel.

The ambiance is consistently positive, and it typically experiences high occupancy during weekends, attracting a respectable clientele.

The cuisine is flavorful, though the portion size is limited to three individuals.
The crispy lotus stem I ordered was quite palatable.

The prawns peri peri, served as a starter, had a modest amount of gravy, and the spice level was customized to my preference.

For the main course, I selected the Chef's Special Chicken Changezi and Birbal Paneer. Both dishes were well-balanced in flavor and not overly spicy.

A wide selection of beverages is available.

The menu also features a variety of continental dishes.

The Dal Tadka is prepared with authentic flavors.

Dessert options include a fresh and flavorful Lotus Biscoff Cheesecake.

A significant advantage is the establishment's 24/7 operating hours.

The pricing structure is also competitive.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

Kanishka Veg Restaurant is a prominent pure vegetarian eatery situated in Mumbai, strategically located near iconic landmarks like the Mahalakshmi Temple and Haji Ali Dargah, making it a convenient dining spot for visitors exploring these spiritual sites. Nestled at 5-B, Haji Ali Circle, Tardeo Road, Mahalaxmi, the restaurant offers an inviting ambiance conducive for family dinners and casual meals alike.¹

Kanishka Veg Restaurant serves an array of delectable vegetarian dishes catering to diverse palates. *Authentic South Indian dishes* like _Sada Dosa_ and _Rava Masala Dosa_ are highlights, delivering *typical South Indian taste* that's true to regional flavors, complemented by flavorful chutneys that enhance the culinary experience. Patrons praise the *tasty dosa*, underscoring the restaurant's knack for capturing traditional essence.² ³

The restaurant boasts a *good atmosphere*, with interiors that are well-furnished and equipped with pleasant lighting, fostering a comfortable dining environment. Reviews highlight *good service*, with staff often described as attentive, friendly, and polite – essential for patrons seeking hassle-free dining, even during bustling festival periods like Diwali and Raksha Bandhan.⁴

Among popular items, diners specifically love *paneer tikka*, *kulcha*, *cheese pulav*, and *fried rice*, showcasing the kitchen's versatility across North Indian and Chinese-inspired vegetarian preparations. *Pav Bhaji* is another crowd-pleaser, available with options like Jain Pav Bhaji, reflecting accommodation for diverse dietary preferences.

On the beverage front, while the *chocolate shake is average*, visitors appreciate refreshing options like lassi – with one reviewer finding the lassi "definitely worth trying – refreshing and delicious!".

Kanishka Veg Restaurant offers a balanced mix of affordability and quality, with price ranges typically ₹200-₹400 per person, making it accessible for varied budgets. Cuisines span *South Indian*, *North Indian*, *Chinese*, *Fast Food*, and vegetarian staples, appealing to those craving familiar comfort food with vegetarian integrity.

Located opposite Haji Ali Juice Centre, proximity to spiritual hubs like Mahalakshmi Temple (0.3 km from Baskin-Robbins, another nearby eatery) and Haji Ali Dargah positions Kanishka Veg Restaurant as a practical choice for visitors blending devotion with gastronomy. Other nearby dining options include Cafe Noorani, McDonald’s Tardeo, and Haji Ali Juice Centre for those exploring alternatives.⁵

Operating hours stretch from *8 AM to 12 AM*, accommodating breakfast through late-night cravings.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil Wadhwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Will surely rate this as 4.5 and above.
First of all Salutations to Shri Pravin Shetty and many thanks to Shri Sudesh Rai as well. Our Wadhwani family have been regular visitors here, ever since our children joined H.M.P.School in 2000-2001. We visited here for lunch today after a long gap of nearly 7/8 years. Pleasantly inviting as always, the management is constantly involved in seating the customers, guiding the stewards and waiters to unattended tables, especially during rush hours, thereby raising the standards of hospitality to a new high.
They have both AC (higher prices) and non-AC sections. Waiting time for AC usually is 15 minutes or more, unless you reach early by 12.15 or 12.30 pm for lunch. We chose the non-AC with good overhead fans, since we were hungry and it was nearly 2 pm.
A heartfelt thanks to Sanjay and his colleagues for the impeccable service provided today and attention to detail.
We had a mix of Cheese Pav Bhaji, Puri Bhaji, Benne Masala Dosa, Rava Masala Dosa and Mysore Masala Dosa with a side order of Sweet Lassi for all.
Each item was served hot, with the regular accompaniments, onion, lime, specially requested pickle, hot sambhar and coconut chutney.
They serve cold Distilled water in Stainless steel glasses, which bypasses the need for any bottled mineral water.
Good quality tissues and an easily accessible washbasin make it convenient for clean up after a finger licking, palate tickling vegetarian meal. Being 100% vegetarian is the added advantage here. They accept all kinds of payments with no extra surcharge or service charges. The regulatory 5% GST is added to your bill amount.
A good hearty meal for five cost us less than 1500 including tips.
Even if you are very hungry and are good eaters, surely you won't spend more than 400-450 per person at this absolutely genuine vegetarian restaurant catering mostly to the College and school kids, especially during day time and the locals living in Andheri West, especially in the evenings.
Valet parking is available.
Latest menu shared here. A separate Fire of Mexico menu, includes Starters, Main course, salads, pasta n rice available . Speciality juices and milkshakes too.

They also provide Home Delivery albeit at slightly higher prices than in-house eating.  Home delivery menu also attached here.

Do visit with peace of mind. Be calm and relaxed. Being hypertensive creates a foul atmosphere for yourselves. Enjoy and return smiling.
